method: Hand-written single-best-answer MCQs grounded only in the accepted open full text.

topic.topicDisplayName: Sjogren syndrome: sicca symptoms, anti-Ro, anti-La, MALT lymphoma risk, systemic features
topic.coverageNote: Covers sicca from glandular hypofunction, anti-Ro, anti-La, systemic disease including ILD, and MALT lymphoma risk.

mcqs.question: How does this review characterize Sjögren disease at the outset?

options.A: A systemic autoimmune disorder with hypofunction of the salivary and lacrimal glands
options.B: A purely local infection of the parotid gland
options.C: A vasculitis that always spares the exocrine glands
options.E: A lymphoma that begins in the lung

mcqs.correctAnswerText: A systemic autoimmune disorder with hypofunction of the salivary and lacrimal glands
mcqs.explanation: Sjögren disease is a systemic autoimmune disorder characterized by hypofunction of the salivary and lacrimal glands.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Sjögren’s disease is a systemic autoimmune disorder characterized by hypofunction of salivary and lacrimal glands

mcqs.question: What does the review say about anti-SSA/Ro antibodies?

options.A: They are present in nearly 75% of patients and play a key role in diagnosis
options.B: They are present in fewer than 5% and exclude the diagnosis
options.C: They are identical to rheumatoid factor
options.D: They are used only to diagnose lymphoma

mcqs.correctAnswerText: They are present in nearly 75% of patients and play a key role in diagnosis
mcqs.explanation: Anti-SSA/Ro antibodies are present in nearly 75% of patients with Sjögren disease and play a key role in diagnosis.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Anti-SSA/Ro antibodies are present in nearly 75% of patients with Sjögren’s disease

mcqs.question: Which antibody finding was associated with increased mortality in the studies this review cites, along with older age and male sex?
mcqs.explanation: Positivity for anti-La/SSB, older age, and male sex were associated with a significantly increased risk of mortality in the cited data.

sourceRefs.excerpt: positivity for anti-La/SSB, older age, and male sex

mcqs.question: What lymphoma risk does the review report for primary Sjögren disease?

options.A: A four- to sevenfold higher risk of non-Hodgkin lymphoma than the general population
options.C: A risk confined to Hodgkin lymphoma
options.E: A lower risk than the general population

mcqs.correctAnswerText: A four- to sevenfold higher risk of non-Hodgkin lymphoma than the general population
mcqs.explanation: Patients with primary Sjögren disease have a four- to sevenfold higher risk of non-Hodgkin lymphoma compared with the general population.

sourceRefs.excerpt: four- to sevenfold higher risk of non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma compared with the general population

mcqs.question: Among non-Hodgkin lymphomas in primary Sjögren disease, which subtype predominates?

options.A: MALT lymphoma, accounting for about two-thirds of cases
options.E: The review says the subtype is never MALT

mcqs.correctAnswerText: MALT lymphoma, accounting for about two-thirds of cases
mcqs.explanation: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma occurs in about 2–9% of patients with primary disease, and the MALT subtype accounts for approximately two-thirds of cases.

sourceRefs.excerpt: mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) subtype accounting for approximately two-thirds of cases
